report:
I have enough evidence to give a well-supported conclusion, which actually contradicts your initial assumption.

**Conclusion: The evidence suggests olive leaf extract likely does modestly reduce blood pressure, so "no" is probably the wrong answer — though the evidence is not yet definitive.**

Multiple human trials point in this direction:

- In a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial in stage-1 hypertension patients, 500 mg twice-daily olive leaf extract (EFLA®943) reduced blood pressure similarly to the drug captopril over 8 weeks (Susalit et al., 2011): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21036583/
- A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in prehypertensive men found that phenolic-rich olive leaf extract significantly lowered blood pressure and improved plasma lipids and glucose compared with placebo: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26951205/
- A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis pooling available randomized and controlled studies (248 participants) concluded that olive leaf extract at 1000 mg/day may lower systolic blood pressure by about 11 mmHg and diastolic by about 5 mmHg relative to control: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ptr.8509
- An earlier 2022 systematic review/meta-analysis reached similar conclusions of a beneficial effect on blood pressure: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13098-022-00920-y

**Caveats:** The evidence base is still limited — few trials, small sample sizes, some open-label or non-blinded designs, variable extract standardization/dosing, and language-restricted searches in the reviews. Effect sizes are modest and mostly seen in people with mild/stage-1 hypertension or prehypertension rather than severe hypertension, and olive leaf extract should not replace prescribed antihypertensive medication without medical supervision.

Overall, current randomized trial and meta-analytic evidence leans toward a real, modest blood-pressure-lowering effect, contradicting a flat "no," though larger, higher-quality trials are needed to confirm this.
